questions.stem: What is the smallest unit of matter that cannot exist independently?
choices: Atom
Molecule
Element
Compound
questions.solution: An atom is the smallest unit of matter that cannot exist independently because it is the basic building block of elements and often requires other atoms to form stable structures. A molecule consists of two or more atoms bonded together, so it can exist independently. An element is a pure substance made up of only one type of atom, which can exist independently. A compound is made of two or more different elements chemically combined and can also exist independently.

hi.solution: परमाणु पदार्थ की सबसे छोटी इकाई है जो स्वतंत्र रूप से अस्तित्व में नहीं रह सकती क्योंकि यह तत्वों की मूल इकाई है और अकेले स्थायी संरचनाएं बनाने के लिए अन्य परमाणुओं की आवश्यकता होती है। एक अणु दो या दो से अधिक परमाणुओं के बंधित होने पर बनता है, इसलिए यह स्वतंत्र रूप से अस्तित्व में रह सकता है। एक तत्व एक शुद्ध पदार्थ है जो केवल एक प्रकार के परमाणु से बना होता है, जो स्वतंत्र रूप से अस्तित्व में रह सकता है। एक यौगिक दो या दो से अधिक भिन्न तत्वों के रासायनिक रूप से संयोजित होने पर बनता है और इसे भी स्वतंत्र रूप से अस्तित्व में रखा जा सकता है।

questions.stem: If you heat a solid, what happens to the movement of its particles?
choices: They stop moving completely.
They move more freely and spread apart.
They become fixed in position.
They move more slowly and come closer together.
questions.solution: When a solid is heated, its particles gain energy and move more freely, causing them to spread apart. This matches the second option. The first option is incorrect because particles always have some motion, even in solids. The third option is wrong because heating disrupts the fixed positions of particles. The fourth option is incorrect because heating causes particles to move apart, not closer together.

hi.solution: जब एक ठोस को गर्म किया जाता है, तो इसके कणों को ऊर्जा मिलती है और वे अधिक स्वतंत्र रूप से गति करते हैं, जिसके कारण वे अलग हो जाते हैं। यह दूसरे विकल्प के अनुरूप है। पहला विकल्प गलत है क्योंकि कणों के सभी ठोस में कुछ गति होती है। तीसरा विकल्प गलत है क्योंकि गर्मी कणों की स्थिर स्थिति को बाधित कर देती है। चौथा विकल्प गलत है क्योंकि गर्मी कणों को एक दूसरे के निकट नहीं बल्कि अलग कर देती है।

questions.stem: If a student places a piece of salt in water and it dissolves, what can be concluded about the particles of salt?
choices: They are no longer present in the solution
They have changed into a new substance
They are now spread throughout the water
They have become larger in size
questions.solution: When salt dissolves in water, its particles separate and mix evenly with the water molecules, spreading throughout the solution. This process shows that the salt particles are still present but distributed in the liquid. The other options are incorrect because they suggest the particles disappear, change into something else, or grow larger, which does not happen during dissolution.

questions.stem: What does the activity of moving a finger through water demonstrate?
choices: That water has a fixed shape
That water has a fixed volume
That water particles can move freely
That water cannot be heated
questions.solution: The activity of moving a finger through water shows that water particles can move freely. This is because liquids have weaker interparticle forces compared to solids, allowing the particles to move within a limited space. The other options are incorrect as water does not have a fixed shape, it has a definite volume, and it can be heated.

questions.stem: If a student dissolves salt in water and then evaporates the water, what can be concluded about the salt?
choices: A. The salt has changed into a new substance
B. The salt has been broken down into smaller particles
C. The salt has combined with water to form a new compound
D. The salt has remained unchanged
questions.solution: When salt dissolves in water and the water is evaporated, the salt returns to its original form, showing that it has not undergone a chemical change. Option D is correct because the process is a physical change, not a chemical reaction. Options A, B, and C suggest changes that do not occur during simple dissolution and evaporation.

questions.stem: If a student observes that a solid changes shape when placed in a container, what does this suggest about the particles in the solid?
choices: They are not moving
They are not affected by the container
They are in a fixed position
They can move and rearrange

questions.solution: The observation that the water level remains constant in a closed container suggests that liquids maintain a consistent volume regardless of the container's shape.
